title: 辰密 (Chenmi): 4 numeric telegrams of Huang Xing's circle, Tokyo <-> Shanghai, 3 June - 13 June 1916 (JACAR)

steps.what: Forms read in columns right to left, four-digit groups; every digit re-read blind by Brice Dudout.
Rongmi and Gongmi keys failed; permuted-page + permuted tens/units model annealed on N13, N16, N26 (201 groups).

The page table found follows the countdown of numbers without a zero, then imposed; 劈 for 力 and 滠 for 灰, both from groups ending 9, gave the rule units 9 = 10; N05 (not in the search, no prefix) then reads through.

Contributor (Wenmi verify.py): the key reproduces every published raw text from the re-read digits; score far above 200 random keys of the same form and 200 digit shuffles. Rerun independently in targets/numeric1916 (20 Oct 2026).
S. Tomokiyo (Cryptiana): the 辰密 key is a 明密 code book with pages, columns and rows renumbered by hand; the contributor checked the exact factorisation over all group values (mingmi.py).
Readings and translations as on the Wenmi page; counted by Daniel's rule: 232 certain, 7 probable, 0 unresolved or illegible of 239.
Project: Dudout's verify.py rerun with python -I (targets/numeric1916/NOTES.md): the 辰密 text scores 3.773 against a maximum of -1.588 over 200 random keys and -1.177 over 200 digit shuffles.

Project: a decoder written here from the key statement alone (targets/numeric1916/decode.py) applied to his digits gives the same character as his published raw text for 239 of 239 辰密 groups. No search for 辰密 was rerun here.

Project, verification 4 (targets/numeric1916/texts/chenmi_reading.md): the four telegrams punctuated from the decoder output; 19 of 19 sentences clean on the explicit-hole rule, 5 holes in 239 characters; grade A.

Project, dating check for the split of numeric1916 (Dan Bourdeau's condition): Dudout's public commits (bdudout/wenmi, UTC) put the 辰密 key on 19 Oct 2026 15:15 UTC; Cryptiana's mingmi section (undated; page 'first posted 18 September 2026, last modified 24 October 2026'; Wenmi cites it as 23 Oct 2026) credits the key formulas to Dudout and adds the reading as a renumbered 明密 book. Recovery predates the section; no priority for the project. Wayback holds only a 2 Oct 2026 capture. See NOTES.md, 'Dating and credit'.

validation.notes: plaintext is Chinese telegraph code numbers, no Chinese letter model in lang; the contributor's verify.py random-key and digit-shuffle nulls were rerun here instead on 2026-10-20 (see solution steps)

outcome.method_basis: Key search scored with a telegraph-code language model, without cribs or plaintext; only the form dates served as checks (key.md, NOTES.md).
outcome.fraction_read_source: Daniel's rule on reading.md: 232 certain + 7 probable of 239 groups (0 unresolved).

gaps.item: 7 characters read as probable (one-digit variants or context)
gaps.detail: Marked {x} in reading.md; the decryption keeps the figure's own value.

credits.note: 辰密: digits re-read on the JACAR scans, key C92 recovered with Claude (Opus 5.5), readings, translations and context

the three keys read as one renumbered 明密 code book (pages, columns and rows rewritten by hand), shown on a June 1916 edition of the 明密碼電報書. The Cryptiana section is undated (page last modified 24 Oct 2026); 23 Oct 2026 is the date Wenmi cites. It credits the formulas to Dudout, whose keys were published 17-19 Oct 2026

texts.label: 辰密 (Chenmi), 4 telegrams, 3 June - 13 June 1916
texts.summary: Four telegrams from Tokyo to the Hunanese group's address in Shanghai (ヒツキン, 277 Avenue Joffre): Shandong and Bo Wenwei; the joint telegram to Li Yuanhong, Cen Chunxuan and the provinces; an elite division under Zhao Hengti for Li Yuanhong; 300 yuan for Jiang Fangzhen.

reading_review.note: Read as sentences 4 Nov 2026 (Chinese, classical telegraphic): all four telegrams read straight through (Shandong offer to Bo Wenwei; the joint telegram to Li Yuanhong and Cen Chunxuan; an elite division under Zhao Hengti for Li; 300 yuan to Baili). 239 groups, 7 probable readings, none unresolved: read, grade A.

prior.where: None known: not in Hsueh Chun-tu's edition of Huang Xing's 1916 drafts (nothing between 8 and 20 June), nor online (Wenmi, Juin 1916 article). 黃興集 and Li Yuanhong's correspondence not yet checked.

human: Brice Dudout read the digits on the JACAR scans (blind re-reading), proposed the reading order of the grids, chose leads and criteria; Claude wrote the solvers, tests and log, proposed hypotheses, readings and translations; Codex made early trials.
